arxiv-2110-06319.title: Continuous Solar Observations from the Ground – Assessing Duty Cycle from GONG Observations Journal: Pub. Astron. Soc. Pacific
arxiv-2110-06319.creator: Kiran Jain, Sushant C. Tripathy, Frank Hill & Alexei A. Pevtsov
arxiv-2110-06319.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kiran Jain, Sushant C. Tripathy, Frank Hill & Alexei A. Pevtsov. Continuous observations play an important role in the studies of solar variability. While such observations can be achieved from space with almost 100% duty cycle, it is difficult to accomplish very high duty cycle from the ground. In this context, we assess the duty cycle that has been achieved from the ground by analyzing the observations of a six station network of identical instruments, Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG).

arxiv-2203-03553.title: Compression of user generated content using denoised references
arxiv-2203-03553.creator: Eduardo Pavez, Enrique Perez, Xin Xiong, Antonio Ortega, Balu Adsumilli
arxiv-2203-03553.description: Abstract Video shared over the internet is commonly referred to as user generated content (UGC). UGC video may have low quality due to various factors including previous compression. UGC video is uploaded by users, and then it is re-encoded to be made available at various levels of quality.

arxiv-2405-03939.title: Long Context Alignment with Short Instructions and Synthesized Positions
arxiv-2405-03939.creator: Wenhao Wu, Yizhong Wang, Yao Fu, Xiang Yue, Dawei Zhu, Sujian Li
arxiv-2405-03939.description: Abstract Effectively handling instructions with extremely long context remains a challenge for Large Language Models (LLMs), typically necessitating high-quality long data and substantial computational resources. This paper introduces Step-Skipping Alignment (SkipAlign), a new technique designed to enhance the long-context capabilities of LLMs in the phase of alignment without the need for additional efforts beyond training with original data length.

arxiv-2408-07695.title: Generalized Quandle Polynomials and Their Applications to Stuquandles, Stuck Links, and RNA Folding
arxiv-2408-07695.creator: Ekaterina Bondarenko, Jose Ceniceros, Mohamed Elhamdadi, Brooke Jones
arxiv-2408-07695.description: Abstract . We introduce a generalization of the quandle polynomial. We prove that our polynomial is an invariant of stuquandles. Furthermore, we use the invariant of stuquandles to define a polynomial invariant of stuck links. As a byproduct, we obtain a polynomial invariant of RNA foldings.

arxiv-2501-04333.title: Gravitational physics in the context of Indian astronomy: A vision document
arxiv-2501-04333.creator: P. Ajith 1, K. G. Arun 2, Sukanta Bose 3, Sumanta Chakraborty 4, Shantanu Desai 5, A. Gopakumar 6, Sanved Kolekar 7, Rajesh Nayak 8, Archana Pai 9, Sudipta Sarkar 10, Jasjeet Singh Bagla 11,17, Patrick Das Gupta 12, Rahul Kashyap 13, Prashant Kocherlakota 14, 15, Prayush Kumar 1, Banibrata Mukhopadh
arxiv-2501-04333.description: Abstract Contributions from the Indian gravity community have played a significant role in shaping several branches of astronomy and astrophysics. This document reviews some of the most important contributions and presents a vision for gravity research in the context of astronomy & astrophysics in India.

arxiv-2506-03090.title: Literary Evidence Retrieval via Long-Context Language Models
arxiv-2506-03090.creator: Katherine Thai, Mohit Iyyer
arxiv-2506-03090.description: Abstract How well do modern long-context language models understand literary fiction? arxiv-2507-07190.title: The Balmer Break and Optical Continuum of Little Red Dots From Super-Eddington Accretion Journal: ApJ Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , Athena++ ( J. M. Stone et al. 2020 ) , FastChem ( J. W. Stock et al. 2022 ) ,
arxiv-2507-07190.creator: Hanpu Liu (刘翰溥), Yan-Fei Jiang (姜燕飞), Eliot Quataert, Jenny E. Greene, Yilun Ma (马逸伦)
arxiv-2507-07190.description: Abstract The physical origin of Little Red Dots (LRDs)—compact extragalactic sources with red rest-optical continua and broad Balmer lines—remains elusive. The redness of LRDs is likely intrinsic, suggesting optically thick gas emitting at a characteristic effective temperature of ∼ 5000 ​ K \sim 5000{\rm~K} .

arxiv-2507-14536.title: Metal-Insulator transition and Charge Transport Mechanisms in SnSe 2 Field-Effect Transistor
arxiv-2507-14536.creator: Aarti Lakhara, Lars Thole, Rolf J. Haug, P. A. Bhobe
arxiv-2507-14536.description: Abstract We report an observation of metal-insulator transition in a thin film of SnSe 2 . The room-temperature carrier concentration of SnSe 2 film was increased by electrostatic doping to 1.14 × \times 10 13 cm -2 . A crossover from insulating phase to metallic state was clearly observed.

arxiv-2509-26489.title: Contrastive Diffusion Guidance for Spatial Inverse Problems
arxiv-2509-26489.creator: Sattwik Basu Chaitanya Amballa Zhongweiyang Xu Jorge Vančo Sampedro, Srihari Nelakuditi Romit Roy Choudhury, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign University of South Carolina
arxiv-2509-26489.description: Abstract We consider the inverse problem of reconstructing the spatial layout of a place, a home floorplan for example, from a user’s movements inside that layout. Direct inversion is ill-posed since many floorplans can explain the same movement trajectories. We adopt a diffusion-based posterior sampler to generate layouts consistent with the measurements.

arxiv-2512-16712.title: Multiwavelength identification of millisecond pulsar candidates in the Galactic bulge
arxiv-2512-16712.creator: J. Berteaud, F. Calore, M. Clavel, J. Marvil, S. Hyman, F. K. Schinzel, M. Kerr
arxiv-2512-16712.description: Abstract Context. The existence of a population of millisecond pulsars in the Galactic bulge is supported, along with other evidence, by the Fermi GeV excess, an anomalous γ \gamma -ray emission detected almost 15 years ago in the direction of the Galactic center. However, radio surveys searching for pulsations have not yet revealed bulge millisecond pulsars. Aims.

europmc-pmc3398752.creator: Marks H, Kalkan T, Menafra R, Denissov S, Jones K, Hofemeister H, Nichols J, Kranz A, Stewart AF, Smith A, Stunnenberg HG.

pmc-10634282.title: MSTL-Kace: Prediction of Prokaryotic Lysine Acetylation Sites Based on Multistage Transfer Learning Strategy
pmc-10634282.creator: Gang-Ao Wang, Xiaodi Yan, Xiang Li, Yinbo Liu, Junfeng Xia, Xiaolei Zhu
pmc-10634282.description: As one of the most important post-translational modifications (PTM), lysine acetylation (Kace) plays an important role in various biological activities. Traditional experimental methods for identifying Kace sites are inefficient and expensive. Instead, several machine learning methods have been developed for Kace site prediction, and hand-crafted features have been used to encode the protein sequences.

pmc-11355267.title: Cranioplasty after Decompressive Craniectomy (DC) in a Patient with Intracerebral Hemorrhage after SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination-Related Vaccine-Induced Thrombotic Thrombocytopenia (VITT)—Proposal of a Management Protocol for This Rare Pathological Condition
pmc-11355267.creator: Lennard Spanehl, Uwe Walter, Thomas Thiele, Daniel Dubinski, Bedjan Behmanesh, Thomas M Freiman, Matthias Wittstock, Patrick Schuss, Hartmut Vatter, Matthias Schneider, Florian Gessler, Sae-Yeon Won, Aldo Spallone
pmc-11355267.description: The COVID-19 (coronavirus disease) pandemic had a severe impact on public health worldwide. A rare but serious complication after administration of adenoviral vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 (AstraZeneca–Oxford and Johnson & Johnson) is vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (VITT), which can lead to serious complications such as cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST).

pmc-11594198.title: Maternal Dietary Improvement or Leptin Supplementation During Suckling Mitigates the Long-Term Impact of Maternal Obesogenic Conditions on Inflammatory and Oxidative Stress Biomarkers in the Offspring of Diet-Induced Obese Rats
pmc-11594198.creator: Catalina Amadora Pomar, Jenifer Trepiana, Irene Besné-Eseverri, Pedro Castillo, Andreu Palou, Mariona Palou, Maria P. Portillo, Catalina Picó
pmc-11594198.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study investigates the impact of maternal nutrition during lactation on inflammation and oxidative stress in the offspring of diet-induced obese rats, along with the potential benefits of leptin supplementation during suckling. Dams were fed either a standard diet (SD), a western diet (WD) before and during gestation and lactation (WD-dams), or a WD switched to an SD during lactation (Rev-dams). Offspring were supplemented with leptin or vehicle during suckling and then fed an SD or WD until four months.

pmc-12430934.title: An Innovative Application of High-Fidelity Medical Simulators to Objectively Demonstrate the Impact of Sports on the Development of Fine Motor Skills—A Pilot Study
pmc-12430934.creator: Peter Szikra, Adam Attila Matrai, Adam Varga, Laszlo Balogh, Zoltan Karacsonyi, Konrad Okros, Tamas Horovitz, Miklos Toth, Norbert Nemeth, Wan-Young Chung
pmc-12430934.description: Highlights What are the main findings? High-fidelity medical simulators with basic training modules can give useful feedback for fine motor skill development.Table tennis has been identified as a sport that can be used to maintain or improve arthroscopy and develop moderate catheter manipulation skills on simulators. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-12553116.title: From Speech Semantics to Brain Activity—Timescales Are Key in Their Information Transfer
pmc-12553116.creator: Saket Kumar, Philipp Klar, Yasir Çatal, Han‐Jen Chang, Friedemann Pulvermüller, Georg Northoff
pmc-12553116.description: Fluctuating timescales are present in nature and are commonly observed in music, movies, brain activity, and speech. In human speech, semantic timescales span from single words to complete sentences and vary throughout conversation. Similarly, the brain's intrinsic neuronal timescales (INT), reflected in temporally correlated activity, carry information across time. How are these semantic and neuronal timescales related?

pmc-12689785.title: Transcriptome and physiological analysis of the response mechanism of Panax ginseng to Benazolin of sulfonylurea herbicide
pmc-12689785.creator: He Yang, Hongyan Jin, Xingmin Dong, Yonghua Xu
pmc-12689785.description: Weeds are among the main pests in the cultivation of Panax ginseng, severely restricting high-quality production. This challenge emphasises the need for effective herbicides suitable for P. ginseng. In this study, P. ginseng grown with benazolin was used to detect digestion dynamics and residual amounts, determine physiological indicators, and carry out transcriptome sequencing.

pmc-12804780.title: Automatic 3D railroad alignment detection using modified Hough transform
pmc-12804780.creator: Jaehyuk Lee, Jeongjun Park, Hyunoh Shin, Hyungchul Yoon
pmc-12804780.description: In railroad infrastructure, timely and accurate maintenance is essential to ensure both safety and operational efficiency. Rail alignment is a critical element for constructing a reliable digital model of railroads. However, conventional rail alignment detection often relies on manual processes that are subjective and prone to error.

pmc-13307385.creator: Hui Liu, Hong Tan, Li Li

pmc-13341123.title: Multicystic peritoneal mesothelioma mimicking recurrent pseudomyxoma peritonei
pmc-13341123.creator: Alessia Scarton, Marco Tonello, Elisa Pizzolato, Carola Cenzi, Ivana Cataldo, Vasileios Mourmouras, Pierluigi Pilati, Antonio Sommariva
pmc-13341123.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Multicystic peritoneal mesothelioma (MCPM) is a borderline variant of peritoneal mesothelioma with indolent behaviour but a significant recurrence rate without radical treatment. Due to its rarity, risk factors and optimal treatment are still to clarify. The present clinical case is a report of MCPM developed after laparoscopic cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (Lap CRS-HIPEC) for pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) of appendiceal origin. The patient was treated for PMP with Lap CRS-HIPEC.

pmc-13458476.title: Lung Function Parameters during Anti-TNFα Therapy in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
pmc-13458476.creator: Maximilian Schulze, Bernadette Schulze, Gero Moog, Serap Alp Bastian, Andreas Bastian
pmc-13458476.description: IntroductionPatients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) may experience a range of extraintestinal pulmonary manifestations. Anti-TNFα therapy has emerged as a crucial treatment option for IBD patients. Despite the pro-inflammatory role of TNFα in pulmonary diseases, anti-TNFα therapy has no major value in their treatment.

pmc-13483461.title: Molecularly defined auditory neuron subtypes show different vulnerabilities to noise- and age-related synaptopathy in mice
pmc-13483461.creator: Joy A Franco, Taylor G Copeland, Ryan D Merrow, Lisa V Goodrich
pmc-13483461.description: Neuronal subtype-specific synaptopathy is a hallmark of many forms of neurodegeneration. We examined the cellular basis for synaptic vulnerability in the auditory system, where three subtypes of spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs)—Ia, Ib, and Ic—carry acoustic information from the cochlea to the brain.

pmc-13604934.title: A qualitative evaluation of asthma patients’ treatment adherence and psychosocial challenges in their daily lives: A phenomenological design
pmc-13604934.creator: Ali Bilmez, Kaan Çakan, Melda Karavuş, Seyhan Hıdıroğlu, Duygu Bağrıyanık, Hamza Ardıç, Mahur B. Aksoy, Mehmet A. B. Çim, Ömer B. Yılmaz, Mohamad Aboras
pmc-13604934.description: BackgroundAsthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease that affects physical, psychological, and social functioning. Treatment adherence is essential for achieving disease control; however, it is often influenced by psychosocial, environmental, and treatment-related factors. This study aimed to qualitatively evaluate treatment adherence and psychosocial challenges experienced by patients with asthma in daily life.MethodsA phenomenological qualitative design was used.
